cap_confirmation: Resolved levels Masquerain 45 (-1), Ariados 46 (0), Lokix 47 (+1), Orbeetle 47 (+1) = cap 48 + offset - 2 throughout.

attempts.notes: Run on work/agent-battle-build-4. Incineroar was KOed by a Lokix Axe Kick and Mega Metagross was taken to 54/150 by two +1 Bug Buzzes before an ally Pollen Puff healed it. Longer and closer than the other two Bug teams.

strategy_checks.check: Ariados redirects to preserve Masquerain's setup or attack
strategy_checks.evidence: Rage Powder on turns 1, 2 and 3. On turn 2 it pulled a 2x Flare Blitz off a sleeping Masquerain and onto itself; on turn 3 it covered the turn Masquerain woke up and got its Quiver Dance. That is exactly the authored job and it cost Ariados its life to do it.

strategy_checks.check: Grass-type powder immunity is the honest counterplay
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 Ariados used Rage Powder and Amoonguss's Spore went straight past it into Masquerain, because Amoonguss is a Grass type. Turn 2's Flare Blitz from the non-Grass Incineroar was redirected normally on the same board. The crack line the dossier names is real and works.

strategy_checks.check: Masquerain does not need Quiver Dance when immediate pressure is stronger, and spends the earned boost
strategy_checks.evidence: It set Quiver Dance on turn 1, was slept, re-set it on turn 3 on waking, and then spent both boosts on Bug Buzz on turns 4 and 5, taking a 150 HP Mega Metagross to 54. The boost was cashed, not hoarded.

strategy_checks.check: Sticky Web requires a damage horizon
strategy_checks.evidence: Sticky Web was never selected at any point, including turn 1 where Ariados had a full four-member team behind it and two grounded reserves still to come. The dossier's warning is about setting the web too late; here the AI never set it at all. See AI defects.

strategy_checks.check: Orbeetle puts both screens up behind Light Clay
strategy_checks.evidence: Light Screen on turn 6 and Reflect on turn 7, in that order, against a board holding a special attacker and a physical Mega. Both went up before it was Spored.

strategy_checks.check: Lokix's Tinted Lens First Impression is entry-only
strategy_checks.result: PASS, and better than the dossier expects
strategy_checks.evidence: On its first entry turn Lokix chose Axe Kick over First Impression - correctly, because Axe Kick is 2x into a Fire/Dark Incineroar and KOed it outright while First Impression would only have been neutral. When Doug later switched the sleeping Lokix out and it re-entered, the AI did select First Impression on that fresh entry turn. The move is being scored on actual damage, not used reflexively.

strategy_checks.check: Swarm on Orbeetle is dead weight on a purely defensive set
strategy_checks.evidence: Orbeetle never used a Bug move and never dropped below 2/3 HP while acting, so Swarm was inert for the whole battle, as the dossier predicts.

protect_ledger.payoff: NOT USED. Three of the four carry Protect and none used it. Ariados in particular spent three consecutive turns on Rage Powder while taking the damage it invited, where a Protect on the third would have bought the same redirection turn for free. No empty guarding, but a clear under-use.

ai_defects.board: Ariados 163/163 on turn 1 with a full four-member team and two grounded reserves (Lokix, Orbeetle) still in the back. Player side: Incineroar and Amoonguss, both grounded.
ai_defects.chosen: Ariados used Rage Powder (and again on turns 2 and 3, never anything else)
ai_defects.problem: Sticky Web is half of this team's identity - the dossier calls the web plus screens 'a genuinely oppressive shell for a route regular' - and it was never set, at any point, in a seven-turn battle. Turn 1 is the textbook case: maximum remaining damage horizon, both player battlers grounded, both opposing reserves still to come. The guard against setting a web too late appears to have become a guard against setting it at all.
ai_defects.better_action: Sticky Web on turn 1, then Rage Powder from turn 2 once the web is banked.
ai_defects.severity: moderate - this is a whole authored mechanic not appearing in play, and the same scoring would affect any other entry-hazard setter

level_changes.reason: First-attempt win with one player faint. Masquerain was the lowest-level member at 45 and is the setup lane the team is built around; it got both Quiver Dances up and still only reached 67 HP before dying to one Ice Punch.

Second-lowest and the member that has to survive for the redirection shell to mean anything. It died on turn 3 having spent every turn protecting its partner. Lokix and Orbeetle are left at +1; both played well.

rerun_after_change: DEFERRED: opponent levels are baked into the headless ROM and this agent must not run make.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep the concept - it is the best of the three Bug teams in this stretch and the darker-mirror framing against Taylor is real, not just prose. Ariados spending its whole life eating attacks for a partner it could not otherwise protect is a genuinely good three turns of play. But the honest answer to 'could this be cooler' here is that the team is currently not playing its own best idea: Sticky Web never appeared, so what the player actually faced was a redirector, a setup sweeper and a screen-setter, which is Taylor's team again with worse Fire resistance. Fix the web scoring before changing any species. If a species change is wanted later, Orbeetle is the slot - a purely defensive body with a dead ability, whose screens arrived on turns 6 and 7 when the fight was already decided. Something like Galvantula or Frosmoth would let the screens support an actual threat. Not changed in this pass.
legality_notes: Authored sets are internally legal. Insomnia Ariados, Tinted Lens Lokix and Light Clay Orbeetle all materialized correctly.
